title: Running A* with a Euclidean Heuristic vs. Dijkstra on a 6-Node Graph
description: Define 2D coordinates and edge weights for nodes A through F, then compare astar from "A" to "F" using h_euclid against h_zero.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import `math`, define the 2D `(x, y)` coordinates `coords` for nodes `"A"` through `"F"`, and specify the weighted adjacency dictionary `edges_undirected`.
Define `neighbors_graph(u)`, `cost_graph(u, v)`, `is_goal_graph(n)` for `goal = "F"`, the straight-line heuristic `h_euclid(n)` using `math.hypot(x - gx, y - gy)`, and `h_zero(_) = 0.0`.

Look at node `"A"`'s neighbors `"B"` (`g = 2.3`, at `(1, 2)`) and `"C"` (`g = 3.2`, at `(3, 1)`). `"B"` has a smaller edge cost `g` from `"A"`. `"C"` lies closer to `"F"` (`(7, 2)`) in straight-line distance `h_euclid`.

steps.question: After expanding `"A"`, which neighbor (`"B"` or `"C"`) has the smaller $f = g + h$ under `h_euclid`, and what happens when `"B"` is later expanded and reaches `"D"`?
steps.answer: `"C"` has $f = 3.2 + \sqrt{17} \approx 7.323 < 8.300$ (`"B"`), so `"C"` pops first (`C -> D` gives $g = 5.6$). When `"B"` pops next, `B -> D` lowers `"D"`'s cost to $g = 4.5$ ($f = 7.662$). This leads to the optimal path `['A', 'B', 'D', 'F']` of cost `6.6`.

steps.description: Run `astar` with `h_euclid` (`expanded: 4`, leaving `'E'` unexpanded) and with `h_zero` (`expanded: 5`), confirming both return `['A', 'B', 'D', 'F']` with `cost: 6.6`.
